'''Thomas Christos Katsouleas''' (known as "TomKat" by students<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dailycampus.com/2022/01/19/carsons-commentary-hey-uconn-whats-going-on/|title=Carson's Commentary: Hey, UConn, what's going on?|date=January 19, 2022|website=The Daily Campus}}</ref>) is an American physicist, engineer, and academic administrator. In February 2019, he was named the 16th president of the [[University of Connecticut]] and officially began his term in August.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.news.virginia.edu/content/uvas-tom-katsouleas-named-next-president-university-connecticut/|title=UVA's Tom Katsouleas Named Next President of the University of Connecticut|date=February 5, 2019|website=UVA Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-news-uconn-president-begins-20190801-cwcr5vxx5ng5pgb2jfo6jedd6a-story.html|title=Thomas C. Katsouleas takes over as UConn president|first=Abigail|last=Brone|website=courant.com|date=August 2019 }}</ref> He resigned the presidency in 2021 and returned to the faculty.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Blanco|first=Christopher Keating, Amanda|date=2021-05-13|title=UConn President Thomas Katsouleas will step down on June 30|url=https://www.courant.com/politics/hc-pol-uconn-president-20210513-7kw5y7o2bzbqbfcvoe3h3xszfq-story.html|access-date=2021-05-13|website=The Hartford Courant}}</ref>

== Education ==
Katsouleas began his undergraduate education at [[Santa Monica Community College]] and received his bachelor's degree from [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1979, earning his Ph.D. in physics from UCLA in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dailycampus.com/stories/2019/2/6/dr-thomas-katsouleas-what-you-need-to-know|title=Dr. Thomas Katsouleas: What you need to know|website=The Daily Campus}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating from UCLA, Katsouleas taught there for seven years before joining the faculty of the [[University of Southern California]] in 1991 as an associate professor of physics. In 1997, he was named a full professor. Katsouleas was vice provost for information services at USC and also was an associate dean of the [[USC Viterbi School of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wraltechwire.com/2008/03/06/duke-picks-southern-cal-professor-as-pratt-school-of-engineering-dean/|title=Duke Picks Southern Cal Professor as Pratt School of Engineering Dean|date=March 6, 2008}}</ref> Katsouleas subsequently served as the dean of the [[Duke University Pratt School of Engineering]] and, beginning in 2015, as provost and executive vice president of the [[University of Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/9664eb3c96314b2a91c913a34751ee68|title=Virginia provost Katsouleas appointed UConn president|last=Eaton-Robb|first=Pat|date=February 5, 2019|website=AP NEWS}}</ref>

On August 1, 2019, Katsouleas became the president of the University of Connecticut; the Greek Orthodox [[Archbishop Elpidophoros of America|Archbishop Elpidophoros]] attended the inauguration ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kokkinidis|first=Tasos|date=2019-10-07|title=Greek Scientist Thomas Katsouleas Installed as President of the University of Connecticut {{!}} USA.GreekReporter.com|url=https://usa.greekreporter.com/2019/10/07/greek-scientist-thomas-katsouleas-installed-as-president-of-the-university-of-connecticut/|access-date=2020-10-01|language=en-US}}</ref> At his inauguration, Katsouleas announced the Connecticut Commitment initiative to cover the cost of tuition for qualified undergraduate and transfer students with household incomes below $50,000. Amid the financial crisis caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the initiative was paused indefinitely in October 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-28|title=Connecticut Commitment Program Paused Amid Budget Challenges|url=https://today.uconn.edu/2020/10/fundraising-shortfall-prompts-pause-connecticut-commitment-program/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=UConn Today|language=en-US}}</ref> Katsouleas also vowed to double research spending at UConn to $500 million by 2030.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Blanco|first=Amanda|date=2019-09-03|title=Doubling research spending at UConn won't be cheap, but new president Thomas Katsouleas says the opportunities are worth it|url=https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-news-connecticut-uconn-pres-20190903-xtv5zl3c4nac3gtgw4ihvpdywa-story.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=The Hartford Courant}}</ref>

Katsouleas announced key initiatives without consulting the UConn Board of Trustees. A rocky relationship with the trustees ensued. Katsouleas was also frustrated at UConn's high fringe rates and unfunded pension liabilities, which he stated made the university less competitive at winning research grants.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Blanco|first1=Amanda|last2=Keating|first2=Christopher|date=2021-05-13|title=UConn President Thomas Katsouleas will step down on June 30; longtime academic clashed with board of trustees|url=https://www.courant.com/politics/hc-pol-uconn-president-20210513-7kw5y7o2bzbqbfcvoe3h3xszfq-story.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=The Hartford Courant}}</ref> Katsouleas resigned as UConn president effective June 30, 2021. He became a tenured professor in UConn's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, earning over $330,000 per year.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Pazniokas|first1=Mark|last2=Thomas|first2=Jacqueline Rabe|date=2021-05-13|title=UConn president has resigned after less than three years in post|url=http://ctmirror.org/2021/05/13/katsouleas-is-resigning-as-president-of-uconn/|access-date=2021-05-13|website=The CT Mirror|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Trustees appointed [[University of Connecticut Health Center|UConn Health]] CEO [[Andrew Agwunobi]] as interim president.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Fawcett|first=Eliza|date=2021-05-19|title=UConn appoints Dr. Andrew Agwunobi, CEO of UConn Health, as interim president|url=https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-news-uconn-interim-president-20210519-4mxviipptjhcvp5oyswnzm6q6q-story.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=courant.com}}</ref>

Katsouleas is an inventor and was awarded the Plasma Science Achievement Award by the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|Institute of Electrical Engineers]] in 2001. He is the author or co-author of more than 200 publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/147174/Thomas-C-Katsouleas|title=Thomas C. Katsouleas|website=NAE Website}}</ref> He was elected in 1996 a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] for "original contributions to advanced [[Particle accelerator|particle acceleration]] concepts including the invention of the Surfatron accelerator, and his detailed studies of beam loading and emittance growth in [[Plasma acceleration|plasma accelerator]]s."<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1996&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Southern+California}} (search on year=1996 and institution=University of Southern California)</ref>

He founded the NAE Grand Challenges Summit in Durham in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thomas C. Katsouleas|url=https://nae.edu/147174/Thomas-C-Katsouleas|access-date=2020-10-01|website=NAE Website}}</ref> In 2010, Katsouleas started Duke's Katsouleas NAE Grand Challenge Scholars Program, which challenges students to use their knowledge to work on challenges posed by the [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ecohusky.uconn.edu/2019/02/12/is-katsouleas-the-sustainability-minded-president-students-asked-for/|title=Is Katsouleas the Sustainability-Minded President Students Asked For? &#124; Office of Sustainability|first=Charlotte|last=Rhodes|date=February 12, 2019}}</ref>
